items.title: Trump could get frosty G7 reception amid confusion over Iran ceasefire
items.description: Conflicting information is being released about the US-Iran ceasefire agreement announced at the weekend, including whether Iran will introduce tolls on the Strait of Hormuz in the future.

items.title: Property market hit by buyer's strike as investors, first home buyers press pause
items.description: Interest rate hikes, tax changes and global economic uncertainty force first home buyers and investors to press pause on property purchases.

items.title: Disaster averted ahead of RBA decision as global oil reserves run low
items.description: Reserve Bank board members will be feeling relieved today when they meet to thrash out our future interest rate movements.

items.title: Feud erupts as consumers on the hook for billion-dollar grid blowout
items.description: Transgrid wants to claw back huge cost increases for a major transmission line from consumers. Experts say the regulator's decision will have far-reaching consequences.

items.title: 'Devastated' family reveals scale of young mother's shark attack injuries
items.description: Leah Stewart was swimming at Coogee Beach when she was attacked just before 11am on Saturday.

items.title: Live: Cabo Verde denies Spain in one of World Cup's biggest-ever upsets
items.description: World Cup debutants Cabo Verde produce an incredible 90-minute performance to hold favourites Spain goalless, taking a point in Atlanta. Follow live.

items.title: Brother believes pregnant 20yo could have been Ivan Milat's first victim
items.description: A family says its private investigation suggests Keren Rowland's 1971 disappearance and death is linked to serial killer Ivan Milat as an inquiry hears claims of missing records, lost exhibits and unanswered questions.

items.title: Senator Duniam's resignation could open door for One Nation
items.description: Tasmanian senator Jonno Duniam's announcement that he intends to leave politics could be the leg up that One Nation needs.

items.title: How Captain Cook went from being celebrated to slain in Hawaii
items.description: Captain Cook set sail from Plymouth to find an elusive trade route linking Europe to Asia in 1776. He never saw England again.

items.title: The AFL teams that are holding their nerve the best in clutch moments
items.description: It's been a season of tight finishes in the AFL, but which teams are holding their nerve the best and why?

items.title: Algal bloom information 'inconsistent', amid survey of health impacts of the bloom
items.description: Volunteers surveyed more than 200 people who reported a range of symptoms during the algal bloom outbreak not represented in the SA government's health advice. A disability advocate says health information has been "inaccessible" and "inconsistent".

items.title: 'Never crossed my mind he wouldn't survive': Seven die daily from drug overdose
items.description: Australia recorded its deadliest year on record for drug overdoses, according to a new analysis, with an average of seven deaths per day.

items.title: Police watchdog set to deliver findings on response to woman's bashing death
items.description: The police watchdog is set to deliver its findings into an investigation of the response to Lindy Lucena's death after her family called for scrutiny.

items.title: Legendary band Australian Crawl reforms for first time in 40 years
items.description: Australian Crawl will lead a major line-up of classic Australian acts across a run of shows later this year.

items.title: Five reasons to try to save cash, even if you're struggling
items.description: Saving is not the only tool you need to achieve financial security these days, but it still has a role to play if you can manage it.

items.title: With the success of 007 First Light, the future of James Bond is looking bright
items.description: While producers are still mulling over who will take the Bond mantle from Daniel Craig, the super-spy has already moved on in 007 First Light.

items.title: Quiz: Can you pick Ireland's flag in a line-up? It's harder than you think
items.description: Which country's flag is the only one with a modern weapon on it? And which US state has the Union Jack on its flag?

items.title: AFP begins inquiry into allegations Israeli forces assaulted flotilla activists
items.description: Australian Federal Police have begun inquiries into allegations that Israeli defence personnel sexually assaulted Australian activists on a flotilla headed to Gaza, following a meeting with Foreign Minister Penny Wong.

items.title: Two men convicted of plot to torch property linked to British PM Keir Starmer
items.description: A Russian-speaking figure who went by the name "El Money" offered one of the men money to torch the properties and take video that could be posted online to draw attention to the attack.

items.title: Hospital call from Melbourne's outer north leaders
items.description: A group of councils in Melbourne's north is calling on the state government to spend $45 million to buy land to begin planning for a hospital and train station.

items.title: Are Australia's environment laws still 'broken'?
items.description: The clearing of koala habitat at a Brisbane school has enraged advocates and raised questions about the federal government's sweeping changes to national environment laws.

items.title: Cairns man charged after allegedly naming man at centre of extortion case
items.description: A Cairns man accused of exposing the identity of a Queensland public figure at the centre of a mysterious extortion case has been charged by police with allegedly disobeying a suppression order.

items.title: Labor's CGT plan flawed but better than what we have, economists tell inquiry
items.description: Economists have offered qualified support for the government's plans on day one of a Senate inquiry.

items.title: PM to make fuel excise call early next week
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says the government will give Australians "appropriate notice" about the fuel excise rebate, as it continues to monitor the issue.

items.title: UK plans to ban social media for under-16s
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer says he will ban social media sites for under-16s and impose restrictions on gaming and live streaming platforms in some of the most far-reaching online restrictions globally.
